minutes.headline: Parks Commission set seasonal beach staff dates and heard Marshall Park funding plan; chair-critical member Dave leaving.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the facilities director's update on parks, the beach house, Marshall Park design and storm damage. It set seasonal employee dates for the town beach, planned an Earth Day cleanup, and discussed skate park paperwork and a possible multi-year funding route for Marshall Park. One member criticised the chair over the recreation director appointment and announced he will not seek re-election.

what_happened.line: The commission voted by roll call, all four members yes, to request that the seasonal beach employee application go to the state with May 8 through September 22, 2023 dates.
The facilities director is to check with staff on a late-June beach opening, weekend openings in June and staying open into early September, then report back.
The chair described seeking one town meeting authorization for Marshall Park with draws as needed, possibly in 2024; a member asked whether that would be excluded debt.
An Earth Day cleanup was planned for April 22 at Wallace Park, with a Veterans Park cleanup April 8.
The commission found no policy on educational use of the town beach, and set its next meeting for April 19.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park's funding route, one town meeting authorization drawn on over several years against borrowing capacity, is a vote residents may be asked to take, and whether it is excluded debt determines whether it raises the tax bill outside the levy limit.
The seasonal dates decide how much of the summer the town beach is staffed and open to residents.
watch_next: Parks Commission meeting on April 19, 2023, with the beach opening and closing dates and any town manager reply on Marshall Park funding.
A possible town meeting article for Marshall Park funding, which the chair said could come in 2024.
